title: Post-Impressionism
description: Bold color and expressive form — the bridge from Impressionism to modern art.

items.title: The Bedroom
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's iconic oil on canvas depicts his modest bedroom in the Yellow House in Arles, France. Known for its vibrant colors, bold outlines, and distinctive perspective, the work expresses a sense of calm and order within his living space.
items.tags: post-impressionism, interior, bedroom, personal, arles, expressive, oil painting, vivid color

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.medium: Oil on artist's board, mounted on cradled panel
items.description_narrative: This striking self-portrait by Vincent van Gogh, painted in 1887, captures the artist with an intense gaze. Executed in oil on artist's board, it exemplifies his distinctive Post-Impressionist brushwork and vibrant palette.
items.tags: self-portrait, oil painting, vincent van gogh, post-impressionism, dutch art, 19th century, portraiture, vivid

items.title: The Poet's Garden
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'The Poet's Garden' is an oil on canvas painting from 1888, showcasing a garden scene rendered with vibrant colors. The artist's distinctive expressive brushwork is evident, bringing a dynamic energy to the natural landscape.
items.tags: garden, landscape, post-impressionism, vibrant, expressive, colorful, nature

items.title: A Peasant Woman Digging in Front of Her Cottage
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh captures a solitary peasant woman toiling in the rugged landscape outside her humble cottage. This painting exemplifies his early focus on the dignity of labor and the harsh realities of rural life in the Netherlands.
items.tags: peasant life, rural scene, dutch art, early van gogh, oil painting, social realism, 19th century

items.title: The Drinkers
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas, painted by Vincent van Gogh in 1890, depicts a lively scene of figures gathered around a table. It exemplifies his distinctive use of vibrant color and expressive brushwork to convey a dynamic observation of everyday life.
items.tags: drinkers, figures, tavern scene, post-impressionist, expressive, vibrant, everyday life

items.title: Fishing in Spring, the Pont de Clichy (Asnières)
items.description_narrative: This vibrant oil painting captures a serene spring day along the Seine, depicting figures engaged in fishing near the Pont de Clichy in Asnières. Created during Van Gogh's time in Paris, it reflects his exploration of lighter palettes and distinct brushwork, influenced by Impressionist and Pointillist techniques.
items.tags: fishing, river, bridge, spring, landscape, post-impressionism, parisian scene, oil painting

items.title: Madame Roulin Rocking the Cradle (La berceuse)
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'Madame Roulin Rocking the Cradle (La berceuse)' presents a vibrant portrait of Augustine Roulin, the wife of the postman Joseph Roulin, whom van Gogh befriended in Arles. Depicting her holding the rope of a cradle, the painting conveys a sense of maternal warmth and comfort.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, post-impressionism, woman, motherhood, arles, dutch art, 19th century

items.title: Terrace and Observation Deck at the Moulin de Blute-Fin, Montmartre
items.medium: Oil on canvas, mounted on pressboard
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's "Terrace and Observation Deck at the Moulin de Blute-Fin, Montmartre" captures an everyday Parisian scene, painted during his early period in the city. Rendered in oil on canvas, the work depicts a specific architectural feature of the historic Montmartre district.
items.tags: Montmartre, Paris, urban landscape, windmill, terrace, oil painting, Post-Impressionism, early work

items.title: The Basket of Apples
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'The Basket of Apples' is an oil on canvas still life, celebrated for its departure from traditional single-point perspective. Executed around 1893, this pivotal work explores multiple viewpoints and complex spatial relationships, influencing the development of modern art.
items.tags: still life, apples, post-impressionism, modern art, oil painting, cezanne, form, composition

items.title: The Bay of Marseille, Seen from L'Estaque
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'The Bay of Marseille, Seen from L'Estaque' depicts the coastal landscape with a structured approach. This oil on canvas work from around 1885 showcases the artist's distinctive style and his frequent subject matter of the region.
items.tags: landscape, post-impressionism, french, bay, marseille, l'estaque, structured, modern art

items.title: Auvers, Panoramic View
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'Auvers, Panoramic View' offers a broad vista of the French village. This oil on canvas exemplifies his early yet distinct approach to landscape painting.
items.tags: landscape, painting, post-impressionism, French art, 19th century, Auvers, modern art, vista

items.title: Madame Cezanne in a Yellow Chair
items.description_narrative: This portrait depicts Hortense Fiquet, the artist's wife, seated in a yellow armchair, rendered with Cezanne's distinctive exploration of form and color. Her solid presence and the structured composition exemplify the artist's shift towards modern art.
items.tags: portrait, post-impressionism, woman, interior, structured, oil painting

items.title: The Vase of Tulips
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's "The Vase of Tulips" presents a vibrant arrangement of flowers in an oil on canvas still life, rendered with his distinctive exploration of form and perspective. Dating to around 1890, this painting reflects his foundational influence on the development of modern art.
items.tags: still life, flowers, tulips, post-impressionism, french art, modern art, painting, contemplative

items.title: The Bathers
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'The Bathers' presents an iconic composition of figures in a landscape, rendered with the artist's distinctive brushwork and approach to form. This oil on canvas masterpiece, created between 1899 and 1904, exemplifies Cézanne's influential exploration of spatial depth and the human figure.
items.tags: bathers, figural, landscape, post-impressionism, french, oil painting, modern art

items.title: The Plate of Apples
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'The Plate of Apples' exemplifies his groundbreaking approach to still life, meticulously exploring form, color, and spatial relationships. This oil on canvas painting showcases his distinctive method of building up forms with visible brushstrokes, transforming everyday objects into monumental studies of structure.
items.tags: still life, apples, fruit, post-impressionism, french art, oil painting, 19th century

items.title: The Three Skulls
items.medium: Watercolor, with graphite, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'The Three Skulls' explores mortality through its stark subject matter, rendered in delicate watercolor and graphite. This late work showcases the artist's characteristic exploration of form and space, even in a somber still life.
items.tags: skulls, still life, post-impressionism, memento mori, modern art, French art, watercolor

items.title: Mahana no atua (Day of the God)
items.description_narrative: Paul Gauguin's "Mahana no atua (Day of the God)" vividly portrays Tahitian figures and a central, seated deity, reflecting the artist's interpretation of Polynesian life. Executed with vibrant colors and symbolic elements, this oil painting captures Gauguin's quest for a more elemental and exotic artistic expression.
items.tags: tahitian, polynesian, symbolism, post-impressionism, spirituality, exotic, figures, vibrant

items.title: Arlésiennes (Mistral)
items.description_narrative: Paul Gauguin's 'Arlésiennes (Mistral)' vividly captures women from Arles under the region's strong wind. Painted in 1888, this work exemplifies Gauguin's distinctive Post-Impressionist style, characterized by bold colors, flattened forms, and symbolic expression.
items.tags: arlésiennes, women, arles, post-impressionism, symbolism, france, oil painting, 19th century

items.title: Merahi metua no Tehamana (Tehamana Has Many Parents or The Ancestors of Tehamana)
items.description_narrative: Paul Gauguin depicts Tehamana, his Tahitian wife, adorned with traditional flowers and a red fan, seated in a contemplative pose. The painting's title, "The Ancestors of Tehamana," hints at a deeper exploration of her heritage and the spiritual world of Tahiti.
items.tags: portrait, tahitian, woman, post-impressionism, symbolism, contemplation, spiritual

items.title: No te aha oe riri (Why Are You Angry?)
items.description_narrative: In this work, Paul Gauguin depicts two Tahitian women, their posture and expressions suggesting the titular question: 'Why Are You Angry?'. Gauguin's use of flattened forms and vibrant, non-naturalistic colors reflects his symbolic exploration of indigenous life and emotion.
items.tags: Tahitian, women, Post-Impressionism, Symbolism, Primitivism, portraiture, contemplative

items.title: Polynesian Woman with Children
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting by Paul Gauguin depicts a Polynesian woman surrounded by children. Created in 1901, the work reflects Gauguin's characteristic style and engagement with Tahitian subjects.
items.tags: polynesian, women, children, post-impressionism, tropical, figurative, painting, tahiti

items.title: Te raau rahi (The Big Tree)
items.description_narrative: Paul Gauguin's "Te raau rahi (The Big Tree)" is a vibrant oil painting on jute canvas from 1891. This work captures a distinctive tree, reflecting Gauguin's exploration of color and form during his time in Tahiti.
items.tags: gauguin, post-impressionism, tahitian art, tree, nature, landscape, vivid, oil painting

items.title: Woman in Front of a Still Life by Cezanne
items.description_narrative: This painting by Paul Gauguin depicts a woman positioned before a still life by Paul Cézanne, specifically his 'Still Life with Fruit Basket' (c. 1888-1890). Gauguin's work highlights his interest in color and form, presenting a dialogue between his style and that of his contemporary.
items.tags: portrait, post-impressionism, painting, still life, female figure, cezanne homage, french art

items.title: Te burao (The Hibiscus Tree)
items.description_narrative: Paul Gauguin painted "Te burao (The Hibiscus Tree)" in 1892, a work that captures the lush environment of Tahiti. This oil on canvas depicts a vibrant landscape, reflecting Gauguin's distinctive Post-Impressionist style and use of color.
items.tags: landscape, Tahiti, tropical, post-impressionism, nature, vibrant, symbolism
